catalog_quote: La palabra fonológica o grupo acentual en macaguán puede estar constituido de dos a cinco sílabas. La sílaba nuclear lleva un acento fonológico, con tono ligeramente alto, así como una ligera duración del sonido nuclear. El acento en macaguán es fonemático, como se puede ver en los siguientes ejemplos: /kénɨ/ '(yo) como' /kenɨ́/ 'uno' (número) /pajál/ 'payara' (clase de pez) /pájal/ 'paila' /néha/ 'tuyo' /nehá/ 'árbol, palo' El tono tiende a ser más alto en las sílabas acentuadas y, en el habla rápida, inclusive la entonación es más alta por toda la oración.

new_statements.quote: La palabra fonológica o grupo acentual en macaguán puede estar constituido de dos a cinco sílabas. La sílaba nuclear lleva un acento fonológico, con tono ligeramente alto, así como una ligera duración del sonido nuclear. El acento en macaguán es fonemático, como se puede ver en los siguientes ejemplos: /kénɨ/ '(yo) como' /kenɨ́/ 'uno' (número) /pajál/ 'payara' (clase de pez) /pájal/ 'paila' /néha/ 'tuyo' /nehá/ 'árbol, palo'. El tono tiende a ser más alto en las sílabas acentuadas y, en el habla rápida, inclusive la entonación es más alta por toda la oración.
new_statements.translation: The phonological word or accent group in Macaguán may consist of two to five syllables. The nuclear syllable carries a phonological accent, with slightly high pitch, as well as slight lengthening of the nuclear sound. Accent in Macaguán is phonemic, as can be seen in the following examples: /kénɨ/ '(I) eat' vs /kenɨ́/ 'one' (number); /pajál/ 'payara (a fish)' vs /pájal/ 'pan'; /néha/ 'yours' vs /nehá/ 'tree, stick'. Pitch tends to be higher on accented syllables and, in fast speech, the intonation is even higher across the whole sentence.

Levinsohn) together with the archive.org scanned and the rendered page scan. The page scan shows printed page 27, '2. FONOLOGIA DEL MACAGUAN', sec. 2.1 'El grupo acentual', and the quoted passage is there word for word, including the accent marks on the minimal pairs /kénɨ/ '(yo) como' vs /kenɨ́/ 'uno' (número), /pajál/ 'payara' vs /pájal/ 'paila', /néha/ 'tuyo' vs /nehá/ 'árbol, palo', and the closing sentence on higher pitch in accented syllables and in fast speech. The scanned text drops the diacrit…
new_statements.rule_in_words: One accented (nuclear) syllable per phonological word of 2-5 syllables, cued by higher pitch and slight length; its position is contrastive (minimal pairs on disyllables with initial vs final accent), and the source gives no rule predicting it.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. Elsewhere in ch. 2 accent interacts with allophony (aspirated stops mainly at onset of accented syllables, p. 35; palatalised /l/ at the end of accented syllables, p. 36; /a/ commonly deleted when the following syllable bears the accent, p. 39).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: 'palabra fonológica o grupo acentual' (2-5 syllables); examples are isolated lexical items in phonemic transcription with the accent mark on the vowel; the orthography (sec. 2.7, p. 40) writes the accent on the vowel as a suprasegmental.
new_statements.identity_note: Source calls the language 'macaguán' and the people Macaguán/Jitnu (sec. 1.1: 'Jitnu' = hit- 'gente' + -nu 'soy/somos'), spoken by ~180 people in Arauca who identify as a mix of Macaguán, Chiricoa, Cuiba and Guahibo subgroups; this is Glottolog maca1259 (Hitnu, ISO mbn) itself, not a differently named variety. No dialects are named.

Accent in Macaguán is phonemic, as can be seen in the following examples: /kénɨ/ '(I) eat' — /kenɨ́/ 'one' (number); /pajál/ 'payara' (a kind of fish) — /pájal/ 'pan'; /néha/ 'yours' — /nehá/ 'tree, stick'. new_statements.rule_in_words: One accented (nuclear) syllable per phonological word of 2-5 syllables, realised by slightly higher pitch and slight length; its position is not predictable from the word shape — it is phonemic, shown by three minimal pairs contrasting initial vs final accent in disyllables. No positional rule is given anywhere in the chapter; cited forms show accent on final syllables (/pa.to.pɨ́/ 'llegué', /mat.bɨ́k/ 'cabeza', /;bɨ́/ 'mucho') and on non-final ones (/bɨ́.ra/ 'sí', /ó.kaɨ/ 'siéntate', /pékn̥a/ 'grande'). Sec. 2.7 (p. 40) lists ´ over the vowel as the orthographic 'acento' mark among the 'rasgos suprasegmentales'.
new_statements.exceptions: No exceptions to a rule (there is no rule). Stress-conditioned detail elsewhere in the chapter: aspirated variants of /p t k/ occur 'mayormente al principio de sílabas acentuadas o sílabas cerradas por oclusivas' (p. 35); /l/ has a palatalised free variant [lʲ] 'siempre a finales de sílabas acentuadas' (p. 36); the [æ] variant of /e/ appears 'siempre en sílabas acentuadas' (p. 37); /a/ is commonly deleted 'cuando la siguiente sílaba lleva el acento' (p. 39).
new_statements.identity_note: Buenaventura 1993 (sec. 1.1, p. 1) describes the Macaguán of Arauca, about 180 people who call themselves 'Guahibo' and are also called Jitnu (from jit- 'gente' + -nu 'soy/somos'); he notes they appear to be a mixture of four subgroups ('Macaguán', 'Chiricoa', 'Cuiba', 'Guahibo'). This matches maca1259 (Macaguán / Jitnu = Hitnü). No dialect subdivision is given for the phonology.
